item.title: Real User Monitoring (RUM)
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Real user monitoring (RUM) measures how an application performs for people using it: how long pages take to load, how quickly they respond, and where users encounter errors.

item.title: Theorem Proving
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: A machine-checked proof that a property holds for all inputs, not just the ones a test happened to exercise.

item.title: Model Checking
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Exhaustive exploration of a system’s reachable states against a temporal property. Where a type checker proves a property holds for one step, and statically checked invariants prove a property holds…

item.title: Static Analysis
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Pattern-matching and dataflow analysis over the source without executing it. Covers the space between a linter (style and local patterns) and a type checker (type soundness): null dereferences…

item.title: Property-Based Testing
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: You state a property that should hold for every input, and the tool generates inputs trying to break it.

item.title: Load Testing
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Does the system behave under the traffic it claims to handle? A load test drives generated requests at a target rate and measures what breaks — latency, errors, throughput — before real users do.

item.title: A/B Testing
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Did users actually behave differently? An A/B test splits traffic between two versions and measures whether the treatment changes a user outcome metric — click-through, conversion, retention…

item.title: Type Checker
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: A Rust compiler saying expected Option<Foo>, found Foo is vastly more useful to an agent than “please reconsider whether this is correct.” This is the first and strongest form of computational…

item.title: Time-to-Repair
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: When this component breaks, how long does it take to restore? A sensor of maintainability measured in hours, not in subjective assessment.

item.title: Synthetic Monitoring
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Scripted user flows run against the production system around the clock: log in, search, add to cart, check out.

item.title: Statically Checked Invariants
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Invariants the compiler refuses to let you violate: Dafny invariant clauses, Frama-C annotations, JML specs, type-level witnesses like NonEmptyList.

item.title: Static Security Analysis
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Attacking the code before it runs. Taint tracking, dataflow analysis, and pattern-based scanners (Semgrep, CodeQL) ask: “is there any path through this program where an adversary’s input reaches a…

item.title: Snapshot Tests
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Did observable output change? Not “is it correct” but “did it change” — a sensor for detecting unintended drift in externally observable artifacts.

item.title: Smoke Tests
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: The cheapest behavioral check against a live deployment: hit /health, create one record, read it back, delete it. If any step fails, roll back.

item.title: Shadow Traffic
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Run the new implementation against real inputs without affecting users. A sensor that produces differential evidence with zero user risk.

item.title: Second-Agent Review
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: An independent agent reviews the first agent’s output. A sensor that applies adversarial pressure to AI-generated code without human-in-the-loop latency.

item.title: Schema Validator
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: Structural coherence at the boundary of the system. OpenAPI/GraphQL schema validation, Terraform plan, Kubernetes admission validation, SQL parser/type checker — all of these answer: is this a valid…

item.title: Runtime Invariants
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: You don’t need to know how the payment service works. You can observe: “5,213 payments occurred; 17 have no corresponding order transition.” That’s a sensor of correctness without understanding the…

item.title: Revert Rate
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: How often does this area get reverted? A black-box sensor of maintainability — you don’t need to understand FooManagerFactoryImpl, you can observe: 27 changes in six months, 8 reverts, 4 incidents…

item.title: Resource Telemetry
item.author: justin@abrah.ms (Justin Abrahms)
item.dc:creator: Justin Abrahms
item.description: CPU, memory, IO, network, GC, queues. Traditional monitoring — useful but limited. Low cardinality, low dimensionality, predetermined questions. Resource telemetry is the weakest runtime sensor.
